Article Title: 'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
Article Text:
Slippages on Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway point to design issue, not construction defect; stretches will need bottom-up rebuild. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Slippages on sections of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway within days of its inauguration point to a design issue, not a construction defect, a top govt official has said, adding that simple patchwork repairs will not solve the problem. "The affected stretches will have to be rebuilt bottom up. We need to ensure there is no laxity at the designing stage of projects. This is a major concern for us, especially since the expressway has been executed under Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM)," the official said.The Centre is awaiting the final report of an expert who conducted a detailed investigation into the slippages. "There was no deficiency in the thickness of the road or in the pavement layers beneath it," the official added. In HAM projects, the private developer is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the project through the entire concession period, which, typically, is 15 years.A preliminary investigation by an IIT Kharagpur professor had identified the use of weak, highly plastic soil beneath parts of the expressway as one of the main reasons for the slippages. Plastic soil loses strength when wet and can get deformed under load. The preliminary report shows poor drainage as a contributing factor.
Article Summary: Slippages on Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway point to design issue, not construction defect; stretches will need bottom-up rebuild. "We need to ensure there is no laxity at the designing stage of projects," top govt official says.

Article Text:

A high-level meeting on the proposed Adaptive Resilience Investment in Coastal Systems on Economics (ARISE) Project was held on Saturday at Lok Seva Bhawan to deliberate on a comprehensive and long-term strategy for protecting Odisha's coastline, enhancing climate resilience and promoting sustainable economic development in coastal areas.Odisha Minister of Revenue & Disaster Management, Suresh Pujari, who chaired the meeting, emphasised the need for a comprehensive approach to coastal management that combines coastal protection, environmental conservation, livelihood security, biodiversity protection and economic sustainability. He stressed that the ARISE Project should contribute towards strengthening the resilience of coastal communities and ecosystems against the growing impacts of climate change.A preliminary assessment of Odisha's 573-km coastline has been undertaken jointly by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA). Consultations have also been held with ADB and the Departments of Water Resources, Forest, Fisheries & Animal Resources Development & Revenue & Disaster Management on key issues relating to coastal erosion, sediment management, protection of coastal villages and safeguarding the lives and livelihoods of coastal communities.Based on these consultations, ADB and OSDMA have prepared a preliminary report, which was discussed in detail during the meeting.It was informed that ADB (Asian Development Bank) has also been working with the State Governments of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu on coastal protection initiatives. The first phase of the coastal protection project in Karnataka has already been completed. The Minister informed that after completion of the final assessment and report for Odisha, the ARISE Project would be taken up in a phased manner, with appropriate interventions to strengthen coastal protection across the State.The meeting discussed integrated measures to address coastal erosion along Odisha's coastline. Emphasis was placed on scientific & technology-driven interventions to reduce erosion, protect vulnerable coastal stretches and strengthen long-term coastal resilience.The development of Odisha's Blue Economy was also deliberated upon, with emphasis on harnessing the State's vast marine resources and economic potential in a sustainable and responsible manner. The approach would seek to generate greater livelihood and economic opportunities for coastal communities while contributing to the State's overall economic growth, a release said.The meeting also focused on promoting Climate-Resilient Coastal Tourism in view of the increasing impacts of climate change and natural hazards. Discussions centred on developing sustainable tourism models that balance economic opportunities with environmental conservation and strengthen the resilience of coastal tourism infrastructure and communities.Coastal Protection and Sediment Management were identified as key components of the proposed interventions. The meeting emphasised the need to understand the natural dynamics of Odisha's coastline and adopt scientifically informed approaches for managing sediment movement and deposition. Strengthening natural coastal defence systems and undertaking suitable protective measures at vulnerable locations were also discussed.For effective implementation of the ARISE Project, special emphasis was laid on Institutional Strengthening, Capacity Building and Advanced Technological Systems. The meeting discussed strengthening the institutional capacity of departments and agencies involved in coastal management, enhancing the technical skills of officials and personnel, and promoting knowledge and experience sharing among stakeholders.The use of modern technology, real-time data and digital platforms for effective coastal management was also emphasised. An integrated technological monitoring system for tracking coastal erosion, improving hazard forecasting, supporting data-driven decision-making and strengthening preparedness and response mechanisms was identified as an important component of the long-term strategy, a release further said.The meeting emphasised that the ARISE Project should adopt a long-term, scientific, integrated and sustainable approach to enhance climate resilience along Odisha's extensive coastline while simultaneously strengthening environmental protection, disaster resilience, coastal livelihoods and economic development.Special Relief Commissioner and Managing Director, OSDMA, Rajesh Prabhakar Patil, senior officials of OSDMA and senior officials of the Asian Development Bank attended the meeting, a release added.
Article Summary: High-level meeting held on proposed Adaptive Resilience Investment in Coastal Systems on Economics (ARISE) Project. Minister of Revenue & Disaster Management, Suresh Pujari, who chaired the meeting emphasised the need for a comprehensive approach to coastal management.

NEW DELHI: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on Saturday and sought each other's resignation.The controversy began after Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) president and Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi's son, Santosh Kumar Suman, sought a review of the quota policy, backing the sub-categorisation of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the reservation regime.“I think the purpose of reservation has not been served. The concept of creating the Mahadalit category with 18 of the 22 Dalit caste groups has been defeated due to the wide gap among the beneficiaries. The Extremely Backward Classes (EBC) category was created out of the other backward castes (OBCs), and the same was true for the concept of economically weaker sections (EWS) among the upper castes,” Suman had said.“How can it be wrong to ask which sections have benefited from reservation and to what extent, and which people standing at the very bottom of the social ladder remain deprived of it? Why is no DM or SP from the Musahar community, which has 4 percent population in Bihar? A comparative study is needed.Why will one section get 8 percent and another 80 percent among the beneficiaries?” he added.The remarks, however, did not sit well with another NDA ally, Chirag Paswan. The Union minister of food processing industries said that if Manjhi and his son want sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then the Union minister should resign."People ask, 'Why isn't there a 'creamy layer' provision?' Well, let them give it up, then - let them stop availing the benefits of reservation," Chirag said."If Jitan Ram Manjhi feels these measures should be implemented, should he not resign first? Let him introduce the 'creamy layer' concept - after all, he would fall under that category too, wouldn't he? He should resign, and his son - who is present here - should resign as well," he added.He also asserted that the basis of reservation lies in social factors and discussing it from an economic perspective "goes against the Constitution.""The basis is social - specifically, the issue of untouchability within society," he said.Later in the day, Jitan Ram Manjhi slammed his cabinet colleague, accusing him of not caring about poor people."People will end up being deprived of the benefits of reservation because of this stance. However, we maintain that this division is essential in the broader public interest."Since he (Chirag) does not want to look after the interests of our poor people, he should resign," he added.The controversy stems from a 2024 Supreme Court judgment that allowed states to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to ensure that the benefits of reservation reach the more backward groups within these categories.It also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the ‘creamy layer’ among SCs and STs from availing reservation.The Centre, however, told the Supreme Court in an affidavit that the creamy layer principle cannot be extended to SCs and STs. It said the principle currently applies only to Other Backward Classes (OBCs)."It has nowhere specifically been held that the principle of creamy layer is applicable to SCs and STs. The reference made to the concept of creamy layer… appears to be the general observation with regard to reservation in respect of OBCs (Other Backward Classes)/SEBCs (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes)."

Article Title: No place in Hindu thought for excluding Muslims: Bhagwat in New York

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday placed Hindu inclusiveness and society-led political change at the centre of his closely watched address at Madison Square Garden, saying a Hindu who wanted India without Muslims would “not remain Hindu” and arguing that public opinion—not political power—was the starting point for lasting change.Bhagwat said the RSS wanted to influence policies, prevent conflicts and “stop wars”, but could not begin by seeking political influence. “Politics has now become a game of self-interest,” he said. Change, he argued, must start in society and create a public view that governments cannot disregard. “If there is public opinion, then no politician will dare to go against it,” he said.Speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration” at the Infosys Theatre in Madison Square Garden, Bhagwat said religions were different routes to the same truth. Rituals and religious discipline were necessary, he said, but they should not become more important than the larger goal of reaching the divine.“Diversity is a decoration for our humanity,” he said, adding that it must be “accepted, respected and protected”. While diversity was the rule of nature, unity was the truth behind it, he said.Bhagwat recalled being asked by Muslims during a 2018 lecture series in Delhi whether the RSS’s idea of a Hindu Rashtra meant they would be driven out.“I said, no. That is not Hindu. If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu,” he said. Hindu thought, he added, required acceptance that different paths could lead to the same truth and that every human being had equal dignity.He said the RSS had since continued dialogues with Muslims and Christians, even though results had been slow. Dialogue and service, he said, must proceed together. He cited the organisation’s 1.3 lakh service projects and said assistance was provided without religious discrimination.Bhagwat also addressed questions about the RSS’s public image. The organisation, he said, was once “minuscule” and ignored but had acquired “some say” in Indian society over its 100-year journey. He blamed doubts about it on “wrong narratives” and said they would disappear if people saw the organisation from within.Calling for work at the local level, he asked religious and community leaders to create examples of unity and selfless service in their own countries and gradually take the dialogue to provinces, districts and smaller communities. Changing entrenched attitudes would be “laborious, tedious and time-consuming”, he acknowledged, urging participants not to abandon dialogue because it produced no immediate result. “RSS with all its might is always with you,” he said.The address came after days of controversy around the centenary-year event, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and supported by more than 200 Hindu American organisations. New York mayor Zohran Mamdani opposed the gathering, describing the RSS’s vision as exclusionary, but acknowledged that the city might not have the authority to cancel a private event.A coalition of civil-rights, interfaith and community groups sought its cancellation, while USCIRF called for Bhagwat’s visa to be revoked and sanctions considered against RSS members. India rejected the commission’s remarks as biased. AHEAD’s X account was briefly suspended and later restored. American singer Mary Millben and BJP spokesperson Nalin Kohli separately criticised Mamdani, arguing that opposing the event contradicted his stated commitment to pluralism.

SRINAGAR: Ladakh is poised for a bespoke constitutional shield, with MHA putting the final touches to a special Article 371 framework for the Union territory, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said.PM Narendra Modi will visit Ladakh to share his views on the proposed framework with people, Rijiju said Friday at a function at Druk Padma Karpo School in Leh district.“Autonomous hill development councils and other existing arrangements are not as empowered. So, recent announcement made by home minister Amit Shah to provide a special provision for Ladakh under Article 371 is going to take shape with the blessings of PM Narendra Modi,” Rijiju said.Unlike Article 370, which gave J&K a high degree of autonomy before its abrogation in 2019, Article 371 provides special, temporary and transitional provisions for balanced regional development and protection of tribal cultures, customary laws and local employment.The proposed Ladakh model is being framed as a “sui generis” governance arrangement. It is expected to offer administrative flexibility and safeguards for tribal land, environment, traditional practices and jobs without granting statehood or directly bringing the region under Sixth Schedule.Rijiju said the provisions would include seven councils, matching Ladakh’s expanded district map. “Earlier, Ladakh had only two districts. Leh and Kargil. Now there are seven districts and along with them there will be seven councils,” he said.Ladakhi representatives from Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the region’s two major political groupings, have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for constitutional safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment. Next round of talks is scheduled for Sept in New Delhi.Rijiju said Modi had long believed Ladakh needed special attention and had worked towards its development since taking office in 2014. He said the region’s transformation had been striking, pointing to roads, electricity, water, mobile connectivity and telecommunications that were largely absent a couple of decades ago.“When we were in university, and later when I became an MP in 2004, I came to Ladakh,” he said. “There were no roads, electricity, water or other basic facilities. Today, the situation has changed. With mobile phones available everywhere, vast road network, telecommunication facility, we no longer have to wonder how long it takes to travel from one part of Ladakh to another.”

At the same time, the upgradation of Kasturba Gandhi schools is also underway," CM Yogi said.He said Abhyudaya coaching facilities were being arranged to help young people prepare for competitive examinations, while basic education schools were being transformed under the government's 'Operation Kayakalp' programme."Arrangements for Abhyudaya coaching are being made for the preparation of competitive exams for the youth, and comprehensive transformations are being carried out in basic education schools under 'Operation Kayakalp', so that the bright future of our children can be advanced," Yogi added.CM Adityanath said these initiatives were aimed at strengthening education, healthcare, infrastructure and opportunities for the youth and establishing new benchmarks of development in Deoria. Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the state has shed its image as a "Bimaru" state. He said Uttar Pradesh now commands a "respectable image" due to improvements in healthcare, connectivity, education and law and order. He laid the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth ₹305 crore.

What’s happening in Nepal?

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh Jal Shakti minister Swatantra Dev Singh on Saturday informed that Nepal’s recent flood disaster poses no threat to the state, while stressing that authorities remained on alert.“There is no threat to Uttar Pradesh from the flood disaster in Nepal, but we remain alert every moment and all our flood-affected districts are safe,” Singh told PTI at the district headquarters.Singh said embankments in the state had become safer since 2017 and claimed that flood-control projects were being completed on schedule.“Before 2017, embankments used to breach, and there was heavy damage. After 2017, all our embankments are safe, and projects are being completed on time,” he said.He added that all flood-control projects had been completed and officials and employees remained alert.Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath on Saturday reviewed the flood situation in Ballia, conducted an aerial survey of affected areas and distributed relief material, assuring that no flood victim in the state would be allowed to face any hardship.According to a statement issued by the state government, excessive rainfall over the past few days has caused flooding in 26 districts, affecting more than 1.71 lakh people and 251 villages.The chief minister said relief operations had been expedited, with more than 1,000 people shifted to flood shelters and 447 flood outposts established.Nepal is continuing a large-scale search-and-rescue operation after flash floods and landslides struck the Nepal-Tibet border region, sweeping away villages, roads, bridges and other infrastructure.A glacier collapse on Wednesday sent a torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris into Himalayan river systems, triggering floods that swept through towns, destroyed bridges and roads, and damaged major hydropower stations. More than 600 people have been killed, while over 2,000 remain unaccounted for.Nepal may need between $4 billion and $5 billion to rebuild after this week’s floods, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters on Saturday, with the estimated cost equivalent to nearly a tenth of the country’s economy.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Jal Shakti minister Swatantra Dev Singh on Saturday informed that Nepal’s recent flood disaster poses no threat to the state. Singh said embankments in the state had become safer since 2017 and claimed that flood- control projects were being completed on schedule.

NEW DELHI: Auto-rickshaw and taxi unions in Delhi have opposed the latest CNG price hike, saying drivers are already grappling with rising operating costs and do not want to pass the additional burden on to commuters.Rajendra Soni, general secretary of the Auto Rickshaw Association and Delhi Pradesh Taxi Union, said CNG prices had risen by Rs 10-12 over the past two-and-a-half to three months, while repeated requests for a meeting with the government had received no response."We do not want to burden the people of Delhi. Over the past two and a half to three months, CNG prices have increased by Rs 10-12. We have written several letters to the government requesting a meeting to discuss the problems faced by auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers. It has been one and a half years since the government came to power, but nothing has been done," Soni said.This comes as Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) has raised CNG prices in Delhi-NCR by Rs 3.89 per kg, citing higher import costs of liquefied natural gas (LNG). The revised price took effect on Saturday, taking CNG to Rs 86.98 per kg in Delhi.This is the fifth CNG price increase in the region this year and the first since May, when IGL raised prices by a total of Rs 6 per kg in four phases over 10 days amid a global rise in energy prices during the West Asia conflict.CNG now costs Rs 95.59 per kg in Noida and Ghaziabad, Rs 95.47 per kg in Meerut and Rs 92.01 per kg in Gurugram. Prices vary across states because of differences in value-added tax (VAT) rates.The latest increase is expected to add to pressure on passenger and freight fares across Delhi-NCR, where auto-rickshaws, taxis and a large number of goods carriers rely on CNG.
Article Summary: Auto-rickshaw and taxi unions in Delhi have opposed the latest CNG price hike. They say drivers are already grappling with rising operating costs and do not want to pass the additional burden on to commuters. Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) has raised CNG prices in Delhi-NCR by Rs 3.89 per kg.
